lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Denise Gadelha Rocha | Lesson 7 -- Navigating Uncertainty

listenings.text: A model does not give you a prediction. It gives you a distribution, a shape of what could happen, with a fat and rather ugly tail on one side. That is the honest output, and it is what the technical team hands over. Then something happens on the way to the board. Somebody flattens the distribution into a single number, because a single number fits on a slide and a shape does not. By the second slide it is a base case. By the third it has become a promise that nobody actually made, and the person who built the model is no longer in the room to say so. I have stopped arguing about the number itself. The question I ask now is worth more than the number, and it is this. What would have to happen for this to be wrong? If the answer is a long silence, the number is decoration. If the answer is specific, you are talking to somebody who understands their own exposure.

I spent years learning to sound careful in English, and then I had to unlearn half of it. My test now is simple. Does the careful sentence tell you what the doubt is actually about? If it does, it is doing work. If it does not, it is vagueness wearing careful clothes, and everybody in the room can feel the difference even when nobody names it. So a range never travels alone. If I say between four and seven, I have to say why it is a range and where the movement sits. It depends on the season, or it depends on one contract renewing. A range without a driver is not caution. It is a refusal to think in public. And here is the part that took me longest to accept. Vagueness costs more than being wrong. A wrong number gets corrected once and everybody moves on. A vague one is never corrected, because nobody can say afterwards what it claimed. You simply stop being asked.

extra_audio.text: The limits that we set in February were built for a season we no longer expect. The exposure, which sits almost entirely in the south, has grown by a third since then. What we have not priced in is a year in which two events arrive together. What I need on Thursday is a decision on the threshold at which we review capacity.
